Section B: Education

text: Views on family life, conjugal roles and marriage change over time. This means that family roles
are also changing, for example the increase in child-centredness or the decrease in the cereal
packet family. Some sociologists think that the family is positive for individuals and society whereas
other sociologists are more critical of the family.

Section C: Crime, deviance and social control

text: Education differs across the world and there are many different types of schools. Formal education
is very different to informal education. Sociologists debate what affects educational achievement,
for example home factors and deferred gratification.

Section D: Media

text: There are many different types of crime, for example cybercrime and urban crime. Sociologists
debate why some social groups commit more crime than others and some believe that policing is
biased. Measurements of crime such as victim surveys reveal that a dark figure of crime exists.
